title: The Day of the Two Blue Mittens
skyStory: Second night of the moon in Capricorn, twenty-four percent lit, and it has rearranged Saturn's furniture without asking. Saturn is quietly furious and quietly impressed. Something in the air today is doubled: echoes on the shore, two crows where one should be, reflections that arrive slightly early. Watch for pairs. The sky is in a matching mood and it will not be subtle.

reading: Somewhere today, on a fence post, a railing or a car antenna, you will see a single blue mitten that someone has rescued and perched there for its owner. Take a picture. Do not ask questions. The mitten knows what it is doing.

Here is the twist: Nancy is going to see one too, a different mitten, same shade of blue, same perching posture, and you will both send the picture within the same ten minutes. Don't even scream. The [[Wheel of Fortune]] is simply showing off. Fire Tiger and Wood Rat, two lost-and-found mittens, one sky with a ridiculous sense of humour. Frame it in your mind.
joel.mission: Put one lost thing back where its owner will find it, and perch it at eye level with dignity.
joel.omen: Two crows on one roof, facing opposite directions. You and Nancy are covering the whole sky between you.
joel.elementWhy: two halves of a matching pair

reading: The moon is in your sign one last night and it wants to leave you a parting gift. It is small, slightly damp and blue. You will spot it before anyone else does, because the Wood Rat always spots it first.

When your phone buzzes with Joel's mitten picture, a minute or two after you sent yours, do the full reaction: gasp, hands up, maybe a small spin. This is a ΔΕΣ moment of the highest order and it deserves your best storytelling hands. Afterwards, write down the exact time. [[The Star]] likes a written record, and you will want proof when you tell this story at a party in three years.
nancy.mission: Tell the mitten story to one person today, with full hand choreography, and do not trim it for time.
nancy.omen: A child's lost toy waiting politely on a windowsill. Someone is taking care of small things, and it is noticed.

together.text: Compare mitten photos and decide which one is the braver mitten. Then invent a tiny backstory: where it came from, who lost it, what adventure it is on. Keep the story going all week. By Friday the mittens should have names, rivals and at least one dramatic rescue.

game.intro: Two blue mittens, two towns, one hand each. Don't even scream. The newsroom has stopped the presses.
game.headline: SINGLE BLUE MITTEN FOUND ___, EXPERTS REFUSE TO COMMENT
